title: Praise the process
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you praise someone, what do you praise?
I started with the book's chess example: a father who rejected innate talent and held that a genius is not born but educated and trained. I asked what that implies.
A student said: he is making it possible for anybody to put forth the work and effort necessary to become a genius.

I said: the father praised effort and process, not the person. If you say, you are really good at that, you give an abstract idea of being born good. If you say, I am proud of you, you consistently make the effort and have a process, then you are in control of why you became good.
A student said: constant praise could cap their potential; if you keep saying we have not seen greatness yet, people keep growing.

Another student said: praising the process by which someone got a deal done removes the idea of favoritism. Others feel empowered that they can model the process, rather than think someone has the gift of gab.

I said that you are studying the intentionality of a person and the way they order it, and removing the personality. I called it third-order intentionality, which is my term and needs a person to check it. I said that wanting to be just like a famous person is nebulous and unachievable, but breaking down what they do is achievable.
A student said: celebrate the winning process, not the winning person.
What is a process you could praise this week, instead of a person?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last thing you praised someone for.
Write it again as praise for the effort or process.
Write a process on your team worth modeling.
Write how you will name it in front of the team.
Write what you will stop saying that praises talent.

check.q: What did I say the father praised?
What did a student say praising process removes?
What did a student say to celebrate?
choices: The winning process, not the winning person

recap: Praise the effort and the process, not the person.
